extracted.intended_audience: educators, educational researchers, grant coordinators, and policymakers interested in K-12 teacher grant writing
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-based study identifying factors that motivate K-12 teachers to write grants, obstacles they encounter, and supports needed; teachers were grouped by years teaching, number of grants written, and funding level to detect differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Years of teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of years of teaching (used to categorize teachers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers were categorized into groups by years of teaching to examine whether years of experience distinguished perceptions of motivating factors, obstacles, and needed support. (Questionnaires mailed to 121 teachers; 89 responses, 74% response rate.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of grant proposals written
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of grant proposals a teacher has written (used to categorize teachers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers were grouped by number of grants written; the study found a significant positive correlation between number of grants written and level of funding received. Use as an experience/engagement metric when evaluating grant-writing capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of funding received
rubrics_metrics.description: Level (amount) of prior grant funding received (used to categorize teachers; example bands: $0–$1,000; $1,000–$5,000; greater amounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups based on funding level showed different perceptions: teachers receiving $0–$1,000 perceived assistance needs and obstacles differently than those receiving $1,000–$5,000 or the highest funding group. Useful both as an outcome metric and as a stratifier for perceived needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition from the School District
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivating factor variable labeled 'Recognition from the School District'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study finding: on this motivating factor, teachers with $1,000–$5,000 in previous funding reported needing increased recognition to continue grant writing, whereas teachers with $0–$1,000 more often needed assistance (locating funding sources, budgeting, technical assistance). Treat recognition as a retention/motivation lever that varies by prior funding level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of Funding Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obstacle distinguished between groups of teachers; teachers receiving $0–$1,000 perceived knowledge of funding opportunities as a greater obstacle. Implies that improving awareness/access to funding listings is a key intervention for less-funded teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Budgeting Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers with lower prior funding (e.g., $0–$1,000) perceived lack of budgeting knowledge as a greater obstacle. Corresponding support need noted: assistance with grant budgeting. Training or templates in budgeting are recommended supports for novice/less-funded teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Technical Assistance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perceived as a greater obstacle by teachers with the lowest prior funding. The study also lists 'technical assistance' among needed supports (e.g., help writing proposals, coaching). Institutions should consider providing hands-on technical support to improve success for less-experienced applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance in locating funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Needed support item: assistance in locating funding sources (identified as a need particularly for teachers with $0–$1,000 prior funding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers with minimal prior funding reported needing help identifying appropriate funding opportunities. Practical supports include curated funding lists, alerts, and search assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant budgeting (assistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Needed support item: grant budgeting assistance (identified as needed, especially by lower-funded teachers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents indicated a need for help with budgeting proposals. Guidance implies providing budgeting workshops, sample budgets, and one-on-one assistance as effective supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Difficulties
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers who had received the greatest amount of funding perceived management difficulties as a greater obstacle than teachers with smaller amounts funded, indicating that as funding scale increases, administrative/management burdens become more salient and require different supports (e.g., project management training, accounting support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher questionnaire (survey instrument)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample teacher questionnaire form appended to the report measuring motivating factors, obstacles, and needed supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study used mailed questionnaires (121 mailed, 89 returned). The appended instrument operationalizes the variables above (motivating factors, obstacle variables, needed support items) and could serve as a template for assessing teacher needs in other contexts. Report contains eight data tables and 11 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation: number of grants written vs. level of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding/metric: a significant positive correlation between number of grants written and level of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets experience (number of grants written) as positively associated with funding outcomes; suggests that increasing writing practice/experience may improve funding levels. Use cautiously given sample (northwest Louisiana teachers, n=89).
